name: Should You Repair a Roof Leak Yourself or Hire a Contractor?

mainEntity.name: Can I repair a roof leak myself, or should I call a contractor?
mainEntity.text: Can I repair a roof leak myself, or should I call a contractor?

acceptedAnswer.text: DIY roof leak repairs are usually only appropriate for temporary damage control, not a permanent solution. A leak visible inside the house may be caused by flashing failure, cracked tiles, torn membrane, clogged drainage, or damaged underlayment several feet away from the stain. Climbing onto a roof also creates fall risk, especially on steep or brittle surfaces. In Los Angeles County, sun-aged materials can be fragile, so walking in the wrong spot can create more damage. If you must act quickly, contain the water indoors and document the location of the leak. Then arrange an inspection so the actual source can be identified. A qualified contractor should check the roof surface, penetrations, attic, and drainage path before recommending a repair. A temporary seal may stop the symptom, but it will not fix hidden damage if the leak keeps returning.
acceptedAnswer.description: You can handle very small temporary fixes, such as placing a bucket or sealing a minor exposed fastener, but most roof leaks need professional diagnosis. Water often enters far from where it appears inside. A contractor can identify flashing, underlayment, or decking problems that a surface patch may miss.
